A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVFM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination and citation-format changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on synthetic conditional transport, MNIST–FashionMNIST transfer, and simulated material microstructure dynamics, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations of T-COT-FM and stochastic extensions.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 correct the reported operation order: OT/Sinkhorn coupling and endpoint resampling now precede kernel calculation and interpolant sampling. This is a limited procedural correction; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun. The kernel inserted into Equation (13) was already part of v1's method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic mappings, MNIST–FashionMNIST domain transfer, and spinodal decomposition dynamics. Appendix E.4 newly explains existing conditioning assignments and rotations without establishing changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Kerrigan et al.'s T-COT-FM; Table 2 adds T-COT-FM, T-COT-SFM, and T-COT-SFM with separate conditioning noise. These introduce a relevant external unpaired-conditioning comparator into two central evaluations, substantially extending comparisons beyond the original ablations and paired-conditioning or complete-trajectory references.

E3.justification: The added materials comparisons introduce shared-noise versus separate conditioning-noise configurations, with the latter using sigma_y = 0.01 and matched network architecture. Previously reported splits, training budgets, sampling procedures, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E.6 add an ablation testing separate conditioning noise in T-COT-SFM, supported by Table 2 and expanded error-distribution plots. The earlier kernel-only, batch-size, transport-weight, objective-variance, and image-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting and mean ± standard deviation were already specified in Tables 1 and D.1. Material-error summaries and predictive uncertainty also appear in both versions. Added comparator results use existing reporting practices without a stated increase in runs or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New comparator entries extend Tables 1–2 and Figures 4/D.7, while existing table values remain unchanged. Added material test-error means are 0.901 for T-COT-FM, 0.637 for T-COT-SFM, and 0.329 with separate conditioning noise, versus retained CVSFM error of 0.188. Table 1 also introduces a lower path-energy result for T-COT-FM on 8-Gaussian–8-Gaussian.

T1.justification: Equation (6) corrects the Schrödinger-bridge optimization from min to argmin and fixes the initial constraint from P0 = mu1 to P0 = mu0. Appendix A.2 adds the limiting argument that eta approaching infinity makes alpha approach one when discussing objective equivalence. The existing theorems and principal derivations otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the novelty framing around the conditional Wasserstein distance and places greater emphasis on the OT-based theoretical motivation and stability mechanisms. The central claims about learning from unpaired conditioning, stochastic extensions, and empirical advantages remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly characterizes CGFM as a lower-bound reference for discrete problems and explicitly interprets comparisons with T-COT-FM/COT-FM through the kernel's treatment of approximate conditional transport. Existing discussions of conditioning-marginal assumptions, eta sensitivity, and conditional versus unconditional image quality are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds concrete synthetic-data construction details: Gaussian class assignments, angular segmentation of moons, the rotation, and the continuous-conditioning formula. Appendix E.6 documents architecture matching and conditioning-noise settings for the added baselines. Hardware descriptions and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Already-cited Chemseddine and Kerrigan papers receive more explicit comparisons, including COT-FM's near equivalence to Chemseddine's approach apart from noise schedules. Carlier et al. is added for Proposition 3.1; references to Alfonso et al., Hosseini et al., and Hochreiter–Schmidhuber are removed. The wider literature coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, method motivation, and experimental discussion. Citations change from author–year to numbered format, affiliations are edited, and acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain comparator rows, and Figures 4 and D.7 gain baseline curves and revised legends. Several appendix displays and algorithms move as the document reflows. The other ten figures retain identical image content, and the overall presentation format is preserved.

improvement.justification: The relevant external comparisons strengthen empirical support, while corrected algorithm ordering and explicit synthetic-data construction improve reproducibility. These are limited gains within a largely retained study. Broad superiority wording still needs qualification: v3 Table 1 reports lower normalized path energy for T-COT-FM than CVFM on 8-Gaussian–8-Gaussian (0.063 versus 0.109), although CVFM retains lower Wasserstein-2 error.
